summary: arXiv:2611.17577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed coordination of electric vehicle (EV) charging with the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) keeps EV constraints private but assumes that every participant follows the algorithm. title: LightTAR: Light and Fast Target-Aware Representations for Multimodal Tabular Learning
summary: arXiv:2611.17600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal tabular learning involves classification and regression on tables combining structured numerical and categorical features with unstructured text and images. These unstructured fields are commonly represented by pretrained encoder embeddings reduced with principal component analysis (PCA).

title: Offline KL-Regularized Reinforcement Learning with Stochastic Transitions
summary: arXiv:2611.17603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: KL-regularized reinforcement learning is the objective behind RL fine-tuning of language models, and its data are often collected by the reference policy itself. However, beyond bandits and deterministic transitions, little is known about how much offline data it needs.

title: Neural Simulation-Based Inference for Computational Cognitive Models: A Tutorial
summary: arXiv:2611.17608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computational cognitive modeling is an increasingly essential methodology to elucidate the mechanisms underlying human and animal cognition. title: Joint World Action Models through Differentiable Trajectory Optimization
summary: arXiv:2611.17626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Joint world action models (WAMs) generate future actions and states together, modeling world-action trajectories rather than actions alone. However, trajectory imitation does not ensure that these trajectories are task-effective or consistent with dynamics.

title: A mesh-free deep energy method for phase-field modeling of thermally driven brittle fracture
summary: arXiv:2611.17630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase-field simulation of thermally driven fracture requires resolving localized crack bands whose paths are unknown in advance and thermal boundary layers whose thickness evolves during the transient. Neural energy-based computations of thermal fracture have so far started from defects placed in advance.

title: Classifier-Guided Latent Diffusion for Small-Molecule Generation
summary: arXiv:2611.17650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion models have emerged as a promising class of generative models for molecular design because of their ability to learn complex chemical distributions and support conditional or guided generation. In this work, we investigate a latent diffusion pipeline for property-guided small-molecule generation.

title: Pattern-Based Matrix Analysis Under Permutations
summary: arXiv:2611.17674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-rank approximation captures one important notion of matrix simplicity: a matrix is simple if it is well described by a low-dimensional linear model. This paper studies a complementary notion.

title: Representational Geometry as a Diagnostic for Adversarial Robustness
summary: arXiv:2611.17684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adversarial training is a common technique for making neural networks more robust to small, intentionally crafted input perturbations, and robustness is commonly measured through accuracy under attack. title: Logically Consistent Accurate Forecasts
summary: arXiv:2611.17735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic forecasting systems based on large language models (LLMs) are now competitive with expert human forecasters, but these systems still suffer from a critical limitation: the inability to produce forecasts that are logically consistent. title: Complex Schr\"odinger Bridges
summary: arXiv:2611.17746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion bridges have emerged as versatile frameworks for facilitating transformations between arbitrary data distributions. However, these approaches are hindered by an immense optimization space and its underlying high-order structures.

title: Antidistillation is Cheap: Lightweight Distillation-Resistance via Stylistic Corruption
summary: arXiv:2611.17772v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a highly effective paradigm for transferring capabilities from large language models (LLMs) to smaller, more specialized student models. title: Direction or Magnitude? Learning Scalars over Task-Calibrated Directions
summary: arXiv:2611.17784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) aims to preserve adaptation quality while reducing training costs. We propose SCALAR, which achieves performance comparable to LoRA with substantially fewer trainable parameters, lower peak training memory, and higher throughput.

title: Federated Physics-Informed Thermal Field Prediction Across Unseen Geometries in Distributed Additive Manufacturing
summary: arXiv:2611.17794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In additive manufacturing (AM), each change in part geometry requires a new thermal simulation, which makes design evaluation over many candidates costly. Geometry-aware models reduce this cost by predicting thermal fields on unseen parts with a single learned model, but they assume that diverse geometries are available centrally.

title: Electrocardiographic Imaging via Posterior Sampling under Operator Discrepancy
summary: arXiv:2611.17851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrocardiographic imaging (ECGI) reconstructs heart-surface potentials from body-surface potentials, an ill-posed inverse problem. Diffusion posterior samplers combine a learned prior with an explicit forward operator that they assume to be accurate.

title: Fuse-All MoE Inference Kernel with Load Balancing on TPUs
summary: arXiv:2611.17857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures activate only a subset of experts for each token, allowing large language models (LLMs) to scale parameter capacity without a proportional increase in computation per token. However, intermediate data movement and uneven expert loads limit the efficiency of MoE inference on TPUs.

title: Disentangling Forgetting from Utility: Lightweight LLM Unlearning via Orthogonal Null-Space Projection
summary: arXiv:2611.17864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) pose significant security risks by retaining private or hazardous information, creating an urgent need for unlearning techniques that excise specific knowledge without compromising general utility. However, prevailing fine-tuning-based unlearning methods struggle to achieve this balance, often suffering from computational

title: Process Mining-Enabled Federated Anomaly Detection for the Industrial IoT
summary: arXiv:2611.17869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While federated anomaly detection enables the integration of local data insights across diverse nodes to reduce false positives, it inherently struggles with non-IID data. In practice, industrial IoT plants often operate under varying conditions and experience diverse environmental phenomena, resulting in significant heterogeneity in the monitored ti

title: Protection-Oriented Assessment of Machine Learning-Based Fault Detection in Power Systems
summary: arXiv:2611.17872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning (ML)-based fault detectors are increasingly proposed for power system protection, yet aggregate metrics can obscure the consequences of false and missed trips. title: Delayed Effects of Temporary Weight Decay in Muon Pretraining
summary: arXiv:2611.17876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A temporary optimization intervention can increase validation loss when it ends yet reduce it at the final training budget. We demonstrate this with temporary weight decay in Muon-trained decoder-only Transformers with 162M, 405M, 1.4B, and 3.4B parameters.

title: From Local Prediction Error to Final Outputs: A Theory of Expert Sharing in Multi-Step Reasoning
summary: arXiv:2611.17879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models can share experts across layers or computational steps, pooling training information from different contexts. This can reduce local prediction error, but multi-step systems are ultimately evaluated by their final outputs.

title: Quantum Graph Neural Networks: Architectures, Trainability, and Applications
summary: arXiv:2611.17886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum graph neural networks (QGNNs) apply parametrized quantum circuits to graph-structured data, with the aim of overcoming limits of classical graph neural networks in scalability, expressivity, and long-range information flow. title: TIDE: Reclaiming Lost Performance In On-Policy Reinforcement Learning
summary: arXiv:2611.17924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synchronous, colocated RL post-training of large language models (LLMs) today suffers from severe under-utilization due to long-tail rollouts. Inference engines fall idle waiting for long-tail rollouts or decode at low, inefficient batch sizes.

title: Differentially Private Federated Class-Incremental Learning for EEG Mental State Classification
summary: arXiv:2611.17944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning (FL) under differential privacy (DP) is typically evaluated on large client cohorts, where subsampling and cross-client averaging amplify privacy and smooth injected noise. Personal biosignal applications such as wearable EEG instead involve small federations of a handful of subjects, a regime whose interaction with formal client-l

title: Tracing Knowledge and Reasoning in LLM
summary: arXiv:2611.17461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current evaluations of Large Language Models (LLMs) report performance at the dataset or task level, revealing what a model achieves but offering little insight into the internal processing associated with its performance. We propose a task-centric framework for characterising the model-internal processing elicited by a benchmark.

title: Poetry 'resurrection' from LLMs
summary: arXiv:2611.17464v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In an era where linguistic creativity is challenged by algorithmic authorship, we pose a provocative question: can artificial intelligence (AI) write an infinite poem? title: Creating Steering Vectors via Input Optimisation
summary: arXiv:2611.17481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Activation steering influences a language model's behaviour by adding a steering vector to its residual stream during generation, but it requires white-box access to modify the hidden states at every generation step. title: Benchmarks Don't Talk Back: Learning Through Self-Disagreement
summary: arXiv:2611.17563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A benchmark usually measures a language model alone with a question, and deployment rarely looks like that: answers get contested, and models give up correct ones under counter-reasoning that is itself wrong. title: CamSpokenNLI: A Pilot Resource for Cross-Variety Transfer Evaluation in Cameroon Pidgin English and Camfranglais
summary: arXiv:2611.17573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cameroon Pidgin English (a West African Pidgin English variety) and Camfranglais are widely used in Cameroon, yet to our knowledge, neither has a dedicated spoken Natural Language Inference (NLI) resource. title: Small Open-Weight Language Models for Crowd Decision-Making: Capabilities and Limits of Output-Level Fusion and Linguistic Aggregation
summary: arXiv:2611.17589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small open-weight language models can run crowd decision-making (CDM) on an institution's own infrastructure, which keeps the checkpoint, the inference settings and the opinions under its control. title: What Do Multilingual Self-Supervised Speech Encoders Know About Sentence Meaning?
summary: arXiv:2611.17686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-supervised speech models (S3Ms) have been scaled up to thousands of languages and millions of hours of audio, yet little is known about how these models structure semantic knowledge across languages. title: See Every Block Once: Variance-Reduced Post-Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models
summary: arXiv:2611.17754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Policy gradient methods are widely used to align large language model outputs with human preferences, but the log-likelihoods they require cannot be directly computed in Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs). title: GDP.xlsx: Benchmarking Frontier Models on Professional Workbooks
summary: arXiv:2611.17766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce GDP_xlsx, a benchmark of 70 realistic workplace requests written by professionals in 13 domains, each paired with an expert rubric of binary criteria and with the complete workbook or CSV file it refers to. title: Activation Steering the Nan-Shan in Typhoon
summary: arXiv:2611.17768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Typhoon is an audiovisual installation based on Joseph Conrad's novella, in which Captain MacWhirr steers the steamer Nan-Shan directly into and through a catastrophic storm. title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent
summary: arXiv:2611.17780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frontier LLM agents that query databases with tools are among the most accurate text-to-SQL systems, but per-query calls to a hosted model are slow, costly, and expose sensitive organizational queries to external APIs. title: RAG-FGO: Dynamic Optimization of Query-Rewriting Agents for Generative RAG
summary: arXiv:2611.17788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), query rewriting serves as a core interface that aligns user intent with external knowledge bases, and its effectiveness directly determines overall system performance. title: CarryOn: Learning What to Keep in Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: arXiv:2611.17808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents can coordinate tools and applications to complete complex, multi-step tasks. As their interaction histories grow, effective context management becomes essential for reliable and efficient execution.

title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix
summary: arXiv:2611.17811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by reviewers to highlight weaknesses during the reviewing process, and their outputs often shape the reviews that humans submit. title: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers
summary: arXiv:2611.17834v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI conference submissions grow rapidly, AI reviewers are being considered as an alternative. title: BLiMP-RO: A Benchmark of Linguistic Minimal Pairs for Romanian
summary: arXiv:2611.17836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating grammatical knowledge in language models requires benchmarks that cover diverse linguistic phenomena and are validated against human judgments. We introduce BLiMP-RO, a Romanian minimal-pair benchmark covering 50 grammatical phenomena across ten domains.

title: UltraBERT-JEV: Encoder models for System One Applications
summary: arXiv:2611.17867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study encoder models that pick one of several options in a single forward pass, without generating text. This technical report compares recipes for fine-tuning UltraBERT-380M with one mask per option.

title: MineralExp: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Experimental Design in Real-World Mineral Exploration
summary: arXiv:2611.17931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In mineral exploration, verifying geological hypotheses relies on designing a variety of geochemical experiments. summary: arXiv:2611.17954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human Label Variation (HLV) is increasingly recognised as an informative signal that reflects meaningful differences in how people interpret the same input. summary: arXiv:2611.17963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper argues that the problem of translation functions both as a point of origin and as a normative horizon for contemporary generative AI. title: FEND: Far-End Detection in Outbound Voice AI Calls
summary: arXiv:2611.18050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a conversational Voice AI agent places an outbound call, the far end may be a live person, a voicemail greeting, an interactive voice response (IVR) system, or increasingly another AI system answering on the callee's behalf. summary: arXiv:2611.18067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence has progressed from task-specific systems toward general models spanning perception, generation, reasoning, and autonomous interaction, making reliable evaluation essential for comparison, deployment, and post-training feedback. title: VEPO: Mitigating Multilingual Hallucinations in LVLMs via Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization
summary: arXiv:2611.18096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) achieve strong multimodal performance, yet they remain prone to object hallucination---generating answers that are linguistically fluent but visually ungrounded. title: Contagious Fingerprints: When LLMs Inherit Another Model's Identity
summary: arXiv:2611.18104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The fingerprint by which a classifier recognizes the LLM behind a text is usually treated as a fixed property of the model. title: Folding Language Models into Themselves
summary: arXiv:2611.18113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge distillation usually trains a compact student from scratch, which needs a large amount of data even though the teacher's weights already encode most of what the student has to learn. title: MamaReason: Unfinished Reasoning and Answer Recovery in Clinical Language Models
summary: arXiv:2611.18264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Answer continuation often returns a diagnosis already stated in unfinished clinical reasoning. We study this behavior in MamaReason, adapted from dense Gemma 4 31B, on MamaBench's 217 paired maternal and child-health presentations.

summary: arXiv:2611.18371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly present, but their effects on human users remain underexplored.
